reason: Full independent review of all four SHA-verified pinned files through EOF, the complete candidate, all five concept patches, current concept context, exact quotes, provenance, and Q1/Q2 found the source's main refund, timing, eligibility, and final-dispute distinctions well grounded. Four material qualifications remain in the proposed source/concept result: same-bank-account dispute sequence, USD presentment versus local-currency settlement, active-mandate reuse after a block is removed, and microdeposit notification only when that verification is needed. These are bounded corrections on unchanged evidence pins.
required_changes: Correct the dispute sequence in the source and concept. Candidate source paragraph under Disputes and proof-of-authorization inquiries and proposed payments-ach-direct-debit-subsequent-dispute patch should say the bank-account block follows disputed subsequent payments from the same bank account, not an unrelated second dispute. Replace the concept's still-active 'First dispute: mandate invalidated' wording with a PaymentMethod-scoped statement that a dispute revokes that disputed method's authorization/mandate and reauthorization is required before reuse. This matches new raw 168 and the accepted ACH accept-a-payment candidate's PaymentMethod/same-bank-account distinction; preserve the separate final-dispute versus predecision-inquiry explanation.

Extend payments-ach-direct-debit-definition or add a separate exact-anchor concept patch for current concept line 12, which still says 'Currency: USD only'. State USD is the presentment currency, while the 2026-11-07 page lists local-currency settlement for eligible merchant Stripe accounts (new raw 84-98). Leaving 'USD only' unqualified next to the new definition contradicts that scope.

Add an exact-anchor concept patch for current Blocked Accounts line 53. A block-removal event does not by itself make the payment method reusable: new raw 101-105 requires an active mandate or a newly collected one. The source candidate already preserves this condition; the concept must not continue to say the event alone signals account is usable again.

Qualify the default microdeposit notification in candidate source paragraph under Mandates and blocked accounts and proposed payments-ach-direct-debit-mandate-email patch. A billing email enables Stripe's default emails, but the microdeposit notification is sent if Stripe needs microdeposit verification (new raw 267-272); the current wording can imply both emails follow every supplied billing email. Preserve Nacha's electronic-or-hard-copy mandate requirement and the distinct custom-notification reminder obligation.

shared_update_decisions.reason: The patch fixes the US-only merchant claim but leaves adjacent concept line 12's unqualified USD-only currency statement, which obscures USD presentment versus eligible local-currency settlement.
The patch correctly makes billing email conditional but should state that microdeposit notification is conditional on microdeposit verification being needed.
It separates requested predecision proof-of-authorization inquiries from uncontestable final ACH disputes and retains one evidence submission only on request.
It replaces the unqualified minimum-time claim and exposes both dated contradictions on partial-refund support and processing-time direction without inferring live account behavior.

The proposed wording improves second dispute but must explicitly scope the subsequent disputed payment to the same bank account and replace the neighboring generic first-dispute mandate sentence with PaymentMethod-scoped authorization language.
